metadata.title: Cathie Wood Drops $124 Million on AI Stocks, Dumps AMD

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Cathie Wood's Ark (ARK) Invest made a sharp semiconductor rotation last week, adding roughly $53 million of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and $41 million of Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) while selling about $95 million of AMD (NASDAQ:AMD). The trades suggest Ark remains aggressive on AI infrastructure but is becoming more selective about which chipmakers it wants to own after a powerful sector rally.
Ark Invest manages actively traded thematic ETFs focused on disruptive technologies, including artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, fintech and autonomous systems. Its frequent trade disclosures give investors a near-real-time look at how Wood is shifting exposure across high-growth stocks.
Nvidia was Ark's biggest purchase of the week. On August 28, the firm bought 243,707 shares worth roughly $53 million across five ETFs, including ARKK, ARKW and ARKQ. The buying came shortly after Nvidia reported quarterly results that topped Wall Street expectations.
Ark also bought 112,836 Broadcom shares worth about $41 million and added 162,875 shares of Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS) valued at roughly $30 million, reinforcing its continued bet on AI computing infrastructure.
The more striking move came on the other side of the ledger. Ark sold 201,863 AMD shares worth approximately $95 million, its largest reduction of the week.
That does not necessarily signal a bearish call on AMD. Ark frequently trims positions after strong runs and reallocates capital toward stocks it believes offer better relative upside. Still, simultaneously adding Nvidia and Broadcom while cutting AMD points to a meaningful shift inside its semiconductor exposure.
Ark also sold roughly $20.6 million of Tempus AI (NASDAQ:TEM) and $18.3 million of Twist Bioscience (NASDAQ:TWST) while increasing positions in Cloudflare, Veracyte and several biotechnology names.
Investor Takeaway
For investors, the key signal is Ark's continued commitment to AI infrastructure rather than any single trade.
The Nvidia purchase immediately after earnings suggests Wood still sees upside despite heightened expectations around AI spending. Investors should watch whether Ark continues accumulating Nvidia, Broadcom and Cerebras while reducing AMD exposure.
The bigger question is whether this becomes a sustained semiconductor rotation. Continued Nvidia and Broadcom buying alongside further AMD sales would suggest Ark increasingly favors dominant AI infrastructure suppliers over broader chip exposure.
